description: WFCAM is the wide-field near-infrared camera on UKIRT and the camera used for UKIDSS. These bands are the Z, Y, J, H and K passbands of the WFCAM photometric system published by Hewett et al.
short_description: UKIRT WFCAM ZYJHK passbands (Hewett et al. 2006) and filter curves
facility_description: The United Kingdom Infrared Telescope (UKIRT) is a 3.8 m infrared telescope on Mauna Kea, and WFCAM is its wide-field camera.
notes: Hewett et al. 2006 give the default ZYJHK curves as system throughput from above the atmosphere to the detector (1.3 airmass, 1.0 mm water), normalised to the measured photon count rate. The UKIDSS technical page offers those tables if you wish to produce your own synthetic colours and states no redistribution terms. The arXiv record uses the assumed 1991-2003 licence, which the arXiv reuse page treats as the non-exclusive licence; the stored sentence is from that page and requires contacting the author before further reuse. The numeric curves are therefore not clearly redistributable. J, H and K were made to the Mauna Kea specification; Z and Y are WFCAM bands, so PhotSystem is the paper's name for the set, ZYJHK, not MKO. The acknowledgement is the citation wording on the UKIDSS archive page (http://www.ukidss.org/archive/archive.html), which has no placeholders. The WSA publications page (http://wsa.roe.ac.uk/pubs.html) gives a similar template that ends 'We have used data from the Xnd data release, which is described in detail in XX et al (200X).' and says that for WFCAM data outside UKIDSS or UHS 'we recommend similar wording, but without the reference to Lawrence et al, Dye at al, or the specific data release paper.' Irwin et al. is cited on both pages as in preparation, with no bibcode, so it has no reference key. Casali et al. 2007 is cited by DOI because bibcode:2007A&A...467..777C failed check_refs. about.ifa.hawaii.edu timed out.

acknowledgements.text: The UKIDSS project is defined in Lawrence et al (2007). UKIDSS uses the UKIRT Wide Field Camera (WFCAM; Casali et al, 2007). The photometric system is described in Hewett et al (2006), and the calibration is described in Hodgkin et al. (2009). The pipeline processing and science archive are described in Irwin et al (2009, in prep) and Hambly et al (2008).
